subject: Civil Engineering
title: Concrete Repair and Rehabilitation
description: A fast breakdown of Concrete Repair and Rehabilitation for builders.

hook.text: A 50-year-old bridge deck is spalling. Tear it down or repair it? Repair saves millions.

buildup.text: Patch repairs remove damaged concrete and replace it with new material — bonded to the old.

discovery.text: Cathodic protection sends electric current through the rebar — stopping corrosion in its tracks.

twist.text: Carbon fiber wraps strengthen deficient members without adding significant weight.

climax.text: Electrochemical chloride extraction pulls salt ions out of contaminated concrete — non-destructive.

punchline.text: Repair extends life by decades. Replacement is the last resort, not the first.

quiz.question: How does cathodic protection stop rebar corrosion?
options: It coats the rebar with a layer of protective paint
Electric current reverses the corrosion process, preventing rust formation
It heats the concrete to dry out moisture around the steel

details.summary: Concrete repair restores deteriorated structures through patch repair of spalled areas, crack injection with epoxy or polyurethane, overlay of new concrete or polymer surfaces, and cathodic protection systems to halt reinforcement corrosion.
details.whyItMatters: Global concrete infrastructure is aging rapidly, making repair and rehabilitation a multi-billion dollar industry. Effective repair extends service life by decades while costing a fraction of replacement.
takeaways: Surface preparation through sandblasting or hydrodemolition ensures bond strength
Epoxy injection restores structural integrity across cracks
Cathodic protection uses electrical current to halt ongoing rebar corrosion

faq.question: Why do many concrete repairs fail within a few years?
faq.answer: Most repair failures result from inadequate surface preparation, failure to remove all deteriorated concrete before patching, ignoring the root cause of deterioration, or using incompatible repair materials.

faq.question: What is cathodic protection and how does it stop reinforcement corrosion?
faq.answer: Cathodic protection applies a small electrical current to the reinforcement, making it the cathode in an electrochemical cell. This prevents the anodic dissolution reaction that corrodes steel. Systems use either sacrificial zinc anodes or an external power supply.
